ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, points A, D, and C are on the same straight line, and $\triangle ABC \cong \triangle DBE$. If $\angle A = 60^\circ, \angle C = 30^\circ$, then what is the measure of $\angle DBC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $\because$ $\triangle ABC\cong \triangle DBE$ and $\angle A=60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $AB=BD$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ADB=\angle A=60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ABD=60^\circ$,\\
$\because$ $\angle A=60^\circ$ and $\angle C=30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ABC=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle DBC=\angle ABC-\angle ABD=\boxed{30^\circ}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the diagram, points A, D, and C are on the same straight line, and $\triangle ABC \cong \triangle DBE$. If $\angle A = 60^\circ, \angle C = 30^\circ$, then what is the measure of $\angle DBC$?
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Given $\because$ $\triangle ABC\cong \triangle DBE$ and $\angle A=60^\circ$,\\ $\therefore$ $AB=BD$,\\ $\therefore$ $\angle ADB=\angle A=60^\circ$,\\ $\therefore$ $\angle ABD=60^\circ$,\\ $\because$ $\angle A=60^\circ$ and $\angle C=30^\circ$,\\ $\therefore$ $\angle ABC=90^\circ$,\\ $\therefore$ $\angle DBC=\angle ABC-\angle ABD=\boxed{30^\circ}$.

The required ∠DBC is the angle at point B, formed by BD and BC, and BD is located inside ∠ABC.
Reasoning: From the problem statement, △ABC ≅ △DBE, with the corresponding order A↔D, B↔B, C↔E, so AB = DB. Because D is on AC, ∠BAD is the same as ∠A in △ABC, equal to 60°. In △ABD, AB = DB, therefore the base angles ∠BAD = ∠ADB, so ∠ADB = 60°. Thus ∠ABD = 180° - 60° - 60° = 60°. Also in △ABC, ∠A = 60° and ∠C = 30°, so ∠ABC = 180° - 60° - 30° = 90°. Since ∠DBC = ∠ABC - ∠ABD, ∠DBC = 90° - 60° = 30°.
